pr_title: kvserver: unskip lease preferences during outage
pr_body:
Previously, `TestLeasePreferenceDuringOutage` would force replication
queue processing of the test range, then assert that the range
up-replicated and lease transferred to a preferred locality.

This test was skipped, and two of the assumptions it relied on to pass
were no longer true.

After https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/85219, the replicate queue no longer
re-processes replicas. Instead, the queue requeues replicas after
processing, at the appropriate priority. This broke the test due to the
replicate queue being disabled, making the re-queue a no-op.

After https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/94023, the replicate queue no longer looked for lease transfers,
after processing a replication action. Combined with https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/85219, the queue
would now be guaranteed to not process both up-replication and lease
transfers from a single enqueue.

Update the test to not require a manual process, instead using a queue
range filter, which allows tests which disable automatic replication, to
still process filtered ranges via the various replica queues. Also,
ensure that the non-stopped stores are considered live targets, after
simulating an outage (bumping manual clocks, stopping servers) -- so
that the expected up-replication, then lease transfer can proceed.

Fixes: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/88769
Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/108175)
This passes 5/5k stresses locally, yet fails reliably on CI. I'm investigating further.
`dev test pkg/kv/kvserver -f TestLeasePreferencesDuringOutage -v --stress --count=1000 --cpus=8` passes, CI is still flaky. I'm thinking that this test may be failing due to CPU contention mostly.
Friendly ping @andrewbaptist, I know you're tied up with bigger fish atm.

Sorry for the delay - I missed reviewing this one. I don't love the solution here though as it is fairly convoluted to reason about whether the range will be processed or not. (Also this would have been a good one to see @aadityasondhi way as he just worked on the disabling of queues). The concern I have is that it is like a "double-negative" to determine if a range will be processed. 

I could see a few more elegant solutions if you feel like implementing them.
1) Add a configurable parameter "ValidRangesToProcess" to the queue. Then leave the queue enabled for this test, but restrict the ranges to the ranges for the ranges we care about. This could be a useful mechanism for support cases as well and could apply to all queues. The default would be the `keys.EverythingSpan`

2) Change the disable flag to a disable func. The default func would return the value of queueConfig.disabledConfig, but it could be overridden in tests to have more complex behavior like this test requires.

3) Change the test to just submit this to the queue in a look rather than just 1 time until it succeeds. I'm not sure if this is possible, but would probably be the simplest.

I like the first one the best as I could see us using it in a lot of tests that want to see queue behavior on a specific range. Let me know what you think.

> Sorry for the delay - I missed reviewing this one. I don't love the solution here though as it is fairly convoluted to reason about whether the range will be processed or not. 

I don't think this is convoluted, but perhaps I'm missing something. For testing, this and other tests use `ReplicationManual`, which will disable the queue via testing knobs.

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/3e9b7de0255f64222c9cd6e8e8d7590405e2ab1c/pkg/kv/kvserver/store.go#L1600-L1602

There's a bit of machinery which validates this in the test cluster setup, and disallows running commands unless `ReplicationManual` is enabled like Split/AddVoter etc

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/dc2c52da339a49405815860cbed511d364b7e146/pkg/testutils/testcluster/testcluster.go#L1877-L1879

I think keeping `ReplicationManual` is valuable. We could change the instrumentation underneath to do something similar to what you're suggesting. However, we would also want to enable a way to interact with the queue valid key spans via SQL. I don't think this is an investment we should make right now.

> Change the disable flag to a disable func. The default func would return the value of queueConfig.disabledConfig, but it could be overridden in tests to have more complex behavior like this test requires.

This idea seems reasonable, however it doesn't appear materially different from what is done here. The disabled flag is set not only by the cluster setting, but can also be set by calling `SetXQueueDisabled`, which some tests do explicitly. In order to add this function, we would need to maintain the disabled variable, the filter function and refer to the queue config on init and changes. 

> Change the test to just submit this to the queue in a look rather than just 1 time until it succeeds. I'm not sure if this is possible, but would probably be the simplest.

The replica won't be re-queued if the queue is disabled. It will hit this path:

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/3e9b7de0255f64222c9cd6e8e8d7590405e2ab1c/pkg/kv/kvserver/queue.go#L657-L663

Not fully deflaked here clearly, the extended CI is failing on this test. I can't reproduce it locally but I'll take another look.


EDIT: My bad, unrelated to the PR, the test does appear deflaked.

Should be good for a final check @andrewbaptist.

I've tried to reproduce the failure I saw on CI for a few hours without luck. The problem from the CI logs, is that the replicate queue doesn't re-process the replica after up-replicating (we kill n2 and n3).

```
dev test pkg/kv/kvserver -f TestLeasePreferencesDuringOutage -v --stress --cpus=40 -- --define -gotags=bazel,gss,deadlock
```

Note this is stressing with more CPUs than are available (24), which has shaken out problems here in the past.

As for why it doesn't re-process, I'm not sure. I don't see any reason why it wouldn't. The possible scenarios that it wouldn't are:
1. target is suspect  -- suspect timer disabled [here](https://github.com/kvoli/cockroach/blob/65bc225c96f83b3371fdae63bbb99d50c7c84c57/pkg/kv/kvserver/client_lease_test.go#L980-L980), so shouldn't be possible.
2. target is throttled -- no indication in the logs, this would be logged [here](https://github.com/kvoli/cockroach/blob/65bc225c96f83b3371fdae63bbb99d50c7c84c57/pkg/kv/kvserver/replicate_queue.go#L683-L683).
3. Queue ended with an error (not purgatory err) -- no indication in the logs, this would be logged [here](https://github.com/kvoli/cockroach/blob/65bc225c96f83b3371fdae63bbb99d50c7c84c57/pkg/kv/kvserver/replicate_queue.go#L704-L704)


So I think there's something I'm missing here. In any case, I'm going to see how the PR CI run goes.


EDIT: I think I got a repro, surprisingly without any additional tags. I'm re-running overnight with added logging to get to the bottom of this here.

I finally got this deflaked properly I think. The changes I made from when the PR was approved:

1. Prevent queue processing until the supposed to be live nodes, are considered live from n1. This was causing flakiness, the test bumps the clocks and this causes n1 to temporarily consider nodes unavailable.
2. Assert that the leaseholder is not n1, instead of asserting that there is a valid leaseholder in 'us'. n1 acquires the lease, up-replicates and then transfers away the lease. After this, it is possible for the lease to not be valid, or for `FindRangeLeaseHolder` to incorrectly think `n1` is still the leaseholder, despite it not being so. This is documented on the fn.

ExtendedCI is failing due to [timeout](https://teamcity.cockroachdb.com/viewLog.html?buildId=11695515&buildTypeId=Cockroach_Ci_Tests_Testrace&tab=artifacts#%2Ftmp) on an unrelated test: `TestStoreRangeMergeWithData`. The flake is from liveness being merged away and re-split #104195:

```
initiating a merge of r66:â€¹/System{\x00aaa-testing\x00\x00-/NodeLiveness}â€º [(n1,s1):1, next=2, gen=2, sticky=9223372036.854775807,2147483647] into this range (â€¹manualâ€º)
```

I think this got tested under `race` because of changes touching the replicate queue. In any case, I'm going to merge this PR. The issue is tracked under #104195.

The merge queue is disabled in this test, however it does appear that liveness has been merged away. I'm going to investigate further before merging just in case this is related to the testing filter.

Fails on master for different reasons than 22.2. I'm fixing 22 cause in #103636 but master failure is happening for other reasons.
First is that it doesn't verify if process in enqueue actually succeeds, and it doesn't because it always fails with 'store throttled' error, so we always check against underreplicated range and fail.
If this operation is retried, then we end up in non-conformance situation after upreplication, but I'm not sure why. Someone from allocator might have a better idea.

I'm going to let this issue lapse even though it's flakey on master. I expect it appear through TC-generated issues and fall into our L2 triage queues, but I'll ping @cockroachdb/kv-distribution if they want to get ahead of it anyway.

review_comments: It wasn't guaranteed that the last leaseholder would be n1. Another node could very well have acquired the lease last, e.g., n2 (as it was stopped), before another node acquired the lease.
